scope_note: Nine previously held source pages were revisited. Complete text and five rendered figures support adapted, text-only revision questions with independently checked answers. The publisher collection label does not authenticate an original UTME sitting, paper order, or official key.

items.source_observation: Source gives circular area increasing at 1.5 square centimetres per second and asks for radial growth when area is 2 square centimetres, to three significant figures.
items.question: The area of a circular region increases at 1.5 cm² per second. When its area is 2 cm², how fast is its radius increasing, to three significant figures?
items.explanation: Since A=πr², the radius at this instant is √(2/π) cm. Differentiating with respect to time gives dA/dt=2πr(dr/dt). Therefore dr/dt=1.5/[2π√(2/π)]≈0.2992067 cm/s, which is 0.299 cm/s to three significant figures.

items.source_observation: Rendered figure shows S outside the circle, SP and SR tangent at P and R, angle PSR 36 degrees, and Q on the major arc PR. The source prose incorrectly places S on the circumference; the figure fixes the geometry.

source_figure.transcription: Circle centre C. Tangents from the exterior point S meet the circle at P and R. The angle between the tangent segments at S is 36 degrees. Point Q lies on the major arc from P to R, so angle PQR subtends the minor arc PR.

items.question: From a point S outside a circle, tangents SP and SR touch it at P and R. If ∠PSR=36° and Q is on the major arc PR, what is ∠PQR?
items.explanation: The radii to P and R meet their tangents at right angles. In quadrilateral formed by the centre, P, S and R, the central angle subtending minor arc PR is 180°−36°=144°. The angle at Q on the major arc subtends that minor arc and is half its central angle: 72°.

items.source_observation: Source equation is log(y+8)+log(y−8)=2log3+2log5. Its displayed ±17 answer omits the domain y>8; the adapted choices distinguish the sole real solution.
items.question: For real y, solve log₁₀(y+8)+log₁₀(y−8)=2log₁₀3+2log₁₀5. Which value satisfies the equation?
items.explanation: Both logarithms on the left require y>8. Combine them to obtain log₁₀(y²−64)=log₁₀(225), so y²=289. The algebraic roots are ±17, but −17 is outside the logarithm domain. Hence y=17.

items.source_observation: Source states eight red balls, a white draw half as likely as a red draw, and two draws without replacement. Its posted 8/33 answer counts only red then white; the adapted question explicitly includes either order.
items.question: A bag has eight red balls and some white balls. On one draw, a white ball is half as likely as a red ball. If two balls are drawn without replacement, what is the probability of one red and one white in either order?
items.explanation: There are four white balls because their count must be half the eight red balls. With twelve balls in total, red then white has probability (8/12)(4/11)=8/33. White then red has the same probability. Adding the two mutually exclusive orders gives 16/33.

items.source_observation: Rendered bar chart shows percentage bands 0–25, 25–50, 50–75, 75–100 with respective student counts 3, 5, 3, 8. The source asks for the number scoring at least 25 percent.

source_figure.transcription: Four percentage-score bars are labelled 0–25, 25–50, 50–75 and 75–100. Their heights on the frequency axis are respectively 3, 5, 3 and 8 students. The at-least-25-percent count is the sum of the final three bars.

items.question: A class has 3 students in the score band [0%,25%), 5 in [25%,50%), 3 in [50%,75%), and 8 in [75%,100%]. How many scored at least 25%?
items.explanation: The three bands starting at 25% or higher contain 5, 3 and 8 students. Add those frequencies: 5+3+8=16. The first band is below 25% and is not included.

items.source_observation: Rendered triangle labels A 82 degrees, C 56 degrees and side CB 43.2 cm. The requested side AB is opposite C.

source_figure.transcription: Triangle ABC has angle A marked 82 degrees and angle C marked 56 degrees. The side CB opposite A is labelled 43.2 centimetres. The unknown side AB is opposite C.

items.question: In triangle ABC, ∠A=82°, ∠C=56°, and BC=43.2 cm. Find AB to three significant figures.
items.explanation: The sine rule gives AB/sin56°=BC/sin82°. Hence AB=43.2 sin56°/sin82°≈36.1664 cm, which is 36.2 cm to three significant figures.

items.source_observation: Rendered diagram labels circle radius 13 cm and chord AB 24 cm, and asks for minor arc AB to three significant figures.

source_figure.transcription: Circle with centre O, radius OB marked 13 centimetres, and chord AB marked 24 centimetres. The minor arc between A and B is the requested length.

items.question: A circle has radius 13 cm and a chord 24 cm long. Find the length of the minor arc subtended by this chord, to three significant figures.
items.explanation: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, leaving a half-chord of 12 cm. Half the central angle is arcsin(12/13), so the full angle in radians is 2arcsin(12/13). Arc length is radius times angle: 13×2arcsin(12/13)≈30.5761 cm, or 30.6 cm.

items.source_observation: The visible source terms are 16.54×10⁻⁵−6.76×10⁻⁸+0.23×10⁻⁶. Exact arithmetic gives 1.655624×10⁻⁴; the earlier held audit miscomputed it. The adapted prompt states three-significant-figure rounding explicitly.
items.question: Evaluate 16.54×10⁻⁵ − 6.76×10⁻⁸ + 0.23×10⁻⁶. Give the result in standard form to three significant figures.
items.explanation: Write every term with the same power of ten: (1.654−0.000676+0.0023)×10⁻⁴=1.655624×10⁻⁴. The fourth significant digit is 5, so to three significant figures the coefficient rounds from 1.655624 to 1.66.

items.source_observation: Rendered L-shaped prism has constant 6 cm width, a lower 8 cm-high beam extending 26 cm to the upright, a final 10 cm upright length, and a total upright height of 22 cm.

source_figure.transcription: Isometric L-shaped solid. Front rectangular cross-section is 6 centimetres wide and 8 centimetres high. Its horizontal run to the taller section is labelled 26 centimetres. The tall end is another 10 centimetres long in the same direction and has total height 22 centimetres. The entire solid has width 6 centimetres.

items.question: An L-shaped solid has a constant width of 6 cm. Its lower beam is 36 cm long and 8 cm high. Over the final 10 cm of its length, the solid rises to a total height of 22 cm. What is its volume?
items.explanation: Split the solid into a full lower beam and the extra upper block. The lower volume is 36×6×8=1728 cm³. The added block is 10×6×(22−8)=840 cm³. Their sum is 2568 cm³.
